plotSections.title: Overcharging a heat stone
bullets: Walker asks whether a stone that already has a magical property can take more magic. Plymouth says that in a free state it would be highly unstable, would take a great deal of energy to contain, and could damage the caster or the item; too much energy in an item that cannot hold it will simply fail.
Walker produces his heat stone and a keystone. Plymouth refuses any attempt to add magic to the keystone.

The heat stone only keeps its bearer warm. Plymouth says more fire magic might be poured into it, then examines it: he rolls it over and pinches it lengthwise before handing it back. It works as advertised, but without proper containment any added energy would make it implode immediately. Walker drops the idea.

plotSections.title: Where the heat stones came from
bullets: The party remembers buying the heat stones because it was cold, in one of the -heim lands, on the way up toward Jotunheim and the seeing stones. Plymouth confirms they were bought in Agenheim.

The seller was Nyx Cage the Ice Mage. He would have discounted the stones if the party went to Helheim and stole a peace treaty between the people of Helheim (the goliaths) and the giants. They remember the offer and did not take it.
No one had kept his name. Walker allows that Nyx Cage could be an alias; Plymouth finds the name shady and does not know him.

plotSections.title: The shifted obelisk
bullets: The party is already at the obelisk. Walker had said it was shifted off the ley line. His notes put the mountain to the west and the obelisk to the north, about twenty degrees off the center; the drawings themselves are gone.

Plymouth says they have traveled roughly 5.6 miles. Facing back toward the guild, the ley line sits to the right of the obelisk, about a hundred yards. Walker treats the twenty-degree figure as far too large.

chronologicalEvents: Walker asks if more magic can be added to a stone that is already magical. Plymouth warns that forcing more magic in, especially in a free state, is unstable and can destroy the caster or the item.
Walker shows a heat stone and a keystone. Plymouth forbids adding anything to the keystone and says the heat stone might accept more fire magic.

The party cannot remember which -heim they bought the heat stones in. Plymouth says Agenheim, from Nyx Cage the Ice Mage, who wanted them to steal a Helheim–giant peace treaty for a discount. They never did the job.
Plymouth examines the heat stone and tells Walker not to add magic: without containment it would implode. Walker abandons the plan.

At the obelisk, Walker reconstructs the shift from notes: mountain west, obelisk north, about twenty degrees off center. Plymouth places the ley line about a hundred yards to the right of the obelisk when facing the guild, after roughly 5.6 miles of travel.
